pages.text: A proton in a field B circles at f = qB/2πm, whatever its speed - so an RF voltage at that frequency kicks it across the dees' gap at every half turn. Each turn adds energy and radius; at the edge, R, it has E = (qBR)²/2m. But its mass grows with energy (γ = 1 + E/mc²), its frequency falls, and over its turns it slips out of phase with the RF. Past about 90° the gap decelerates it.
$(thing)Set$(): Magnetic field B, RF frequency, Beam current.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Field ripple: B varies by ±0.05%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The beam has slipped out of phase with the RF; The iron yoke is saturating; The target is melting under the beam.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More current makes the isotope faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective field: B·(1 + δ)$(br)Cyclotron frequency: f = qB/2πm$(br)Beam energy: E = (qBR)²/2m$(br)Turns: N = E/2qV$(br)Phase slip: Δφ = 360°·N·|f_RF·γ/f_c − 1|$(br)Beam power: P = E·I
